Title: Great core gameplay buried under predatory monetization and zero integrity

Rating: 1/5

Apex Legends used to be the gold standard for movement shooters, but at this point, it’s impossible to recommend.

Cheaters everywhere: Ranked is completely unplayable. Every other match features cronus/strikeepad users on console, wallhacks, or aimbotters on PC. The anti-cheat updates feel like band-aids on a sinking ship.

Ecosystem and matchmaking: The skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) is aggressively tuned to keep you on a win/loss hamster wheel. Solo queuing is pure misery—you're constantly thrown into lobbies against pre-made three-stacks sweating like it’s a tournament finals.

Aggressive monetization: Instead of fixing core performance bugs, server desync, and audio glitches that have existed for years, the priority is clearly pumping out absurdly overpriced microtransactions, heirlooms, and gacha-style packs.

Meta staleness: Balance patches take way too long to address broken Legends or weapons, while fun mechanics constantly get gutted in the name of "balance."

The shooting and movement mechanics are fantastic, but everything built around them is designed to frustrate you into spending money or grinding endlessly. Save your time and sanity—play something else.

I am suprised that this game is still going 7 years after release. Like, I haven't met anyone mention this game just casually and yet this game is the 25th most played game on Steam! I played Apex Legends AGES ago, back when they still had gold armor and helmets. So when this game started appearing on my Instagram showing clips of people clutching the most unclutable fights, pulling some random bullshit movement tech that just breaks everyones ankles, or rizzing up japanese baddies? I knew I had to redownload and give this game a proper go!

It was quite suprising for me when I got into my first game back as a lot of things had been added or changed/reworked so I did have to spend some time learning new mechanics, but they were explained pretty well and or pretty simple to use. I remember struggling on the mantle boost but after a few games I had it down to a T and felt pretty good whenever I was able to hit it. So was I able to hit some crazy clips? YES SIR!! I've had a few clutch moments and let me tell you the dopamine high was immaculate, I swear my brain shortcircuited at least once during my time playing this game due to how crazy these fights get. I didn't really get much movement tech down but what I was able to achieve was pretty fun, and I wasn't able to rizz up any japanese baddies, so no tsundere girlfriend for me. But that doesn't matter that much.

I think Apex Legends does a pretty good job at achivements, as a majority of them insentivise you to give each Legend a proper go, and the rest are just unlocked naturally through playing the game. Which was great, as I didn't feel like I was doing a chore and instead was enjoying the game. The only achievement I had to go out of my way for was [b] Decked Out [/b] which is a lot harder to get due to gold armour and helment not existing anymore, but after that? It was just smooth sailing. I felt like I gave every Legend a good chance and got to try a variety of diffrent weapons to see what I liked/didn't like. Speaking of weapons, the gunplay in this game is so satisfying. Each weapon sounds so crisp and you can feel the feedback of each bullet hitting your target. The sound effects are also really good too and you can easily tell what is happening (sometimes) during a fight. My personal favourite weapons are the R-301 Carbine, Volt, Prowler, EVA-8 Auto, Peacekeeper and Triple Take. Each of these weapons both sound good and feel good to hit someone with.

Apex Legends was definitely a suprisingly fun experience for me, from wiping out squads solo to winning games, no matter what happens you will definitely have a good time. The acheivements although quite boring in nature, were pretty much perfect and to me, felt like an obligation to try out each Legend at least once. I even got a heirloom too! Which was the last thing I was expecting to get while playing this game LMAO. So I do think that I was able to experience everything that this game has to offer and I wouldn't mind playing this game again sometime. On a small note, I won the last game that I played as I hit level 50 which feels like the perfect end to my journey for now. Great game, great gunplay, great movement, no tsundere girlfriend.

Every match is a social experiment designed to test how much disappointment a human being can withstand.
My teammates loot like archaeologists, rotate like drunk GPS systems, and fight like they have personal insurance against bullets.
The enemy team? Former special forces. My team? Three unpaid interns fighting over a Mozambique.
I have been killed by people with 3 million kills, 17 different badges, and the reaction time of a NASA supercomputer.
Meanwhile, I miss an entire magazine on someone standing directly in front of me.
The ring is closing. My teammates are looting. The enemy is pushing. My teammates are looting. My existence is collapsing. My teammates are STILL LOOTING.
My teammates have the awareness of a microwaved potato. My aim looks like I'm trying to shoot mosquitoes with a blindfold on. Every enemy squad has the aim of a military veteran, while I can't even hit someone standing still.
I've been third-partied so many times that I'm starting to think I'm the third party.
Would I recommend this game? Absolutely not.
Will I be playing tomorrow? Unfortunately, yes.

The competitive nature of Apex, often marked by its steep learning curve and frequent disappointments, and people using wraith to enter you, can evoke feelings of frustration and inadequacy, making it seem trivial in comparison to the profound challenges faced in real life.
